The rejected promise causes Promise.all to fail, so the catch handler returns failure for all calendar references instead of skipping only the missing credential."

findings.title: Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: mainHostDestinationCalendar can be undefined when evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, but the code accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining. Booking creation using Google Meet without a destination calendar will throw a TypeError instead of falling back to Cal Video.

findings.title: Team destination calendars are dropped when main destination calendar is null
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The later collective-only code uses evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars), so team members' destination calendars are silently ignored. Hosts with connected calendars can miss calendar events.

findings.title: Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event
findings.body: When a newBookingId is provided, updateAllCalendarEvents finds only the first calendar reference from the old booking and deletes that event. Collective bookings can have multiple calendar references, so the other hosts' old calendar events are left behind after reschedule.

findings.title: updateEvent result omits credentialId and externalId needed for references
findings.body: CalendarManager.updateEvent returns an EventResult without credentialId or externalId, but EventManager.updateLocation now builds referencesToCreate from result.credentialId and result.externalId. Calendar references created after an location edit can lose the credential and external calendar linkage.

findings.title: Google update fallback cannot select a calendar when externalCalendarId is missing
findings.body: selectedCalendar is computed as externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId. When externalCalendarId is null or undefined, the fallback searches for externalId === undefined and returns undefined, so updateEvent can call the Google API with an undefined calendarId instead of falling back to the main destination calendar.

findings.title: Google hangout-link patch may use undefined calendarId
findings.body: createEvent inserts the event with selectedCalendar || 'primary', but the follow-up patch to add the hangout link uses selectedCalendar without the same fallback. If no matching destination calendar is found, the patch request has an undefined calendarId and the event description may not be updated.

findings.title: Google delete fallback may target the primary calendar instead of the event calendar
findings.body: deleteEvent uses the same faulty fallback as updateEvent when externalCalendarId is missing and then falls back to 'primary'. If the event was created on a non-primary calendar and no externalCalendarId is stored, deletion can hit the wrong calendar, receive a 404, and silently leave the event undeleted.

findings.title: Organizer email uses the first destination calendar for all host calendars
findings.body: In createEvent, the organizer attendee email is taken from the first destination calendar in the event, while the event may be created on another host's calendar using a different credentialId. For collective events this can mark the wrong user as organizer or send incorrect calendar notifications on non-main host calendars.

findings.title: Lark createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
findings.body: EventManager can invoke createEvent once per host credential for collective events, but LarkCalendarService always uses event.destinationCalendar[0].externalId. Events for additional hosts can either fail because the credential does not own that calendar or create duplicate events on the first host's calendar.

findings.title: Office 365 createEvent always uses the first destination calendar
findings.body: Office365CalendarService.createEvent selects the first entry of event.destinationCalendar regardless of the credential being used. With multiple collective hosts, calls made with another host's credential may try to create the event in the first host's calendar or fail, so non-main hosts are not reliably invited.

findings.title: CalDAV createEvent filters calendars by the first destination calendar only
findings.body: BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters listCalendars results using only the first destination calendar's externalId. When called for another host's credential, no calendar may match, resulting in zero createCalendarObject calls while still returning success; the other host's event is silently not created.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation deletes only the first calendar reference and ignores other hosts
findings.body: In the recurring-cancellation branch, for each updated booking the code uses references.find(ref => ref.type.includes('_calendar')) and iterates only the organizer's credentials. Collective bookings can have multiple calendar references belonging to different hosts, so other hosts' recurring calendar events may not be deleted.

findings.title: Paid cancellation does not await deletion promises
findings.body: The paid cancellation path executes 'await apiDeletes' where apiDeletes is an array of promises. Awaiting the array does not wait for the contained promises, so calendar/video deletions may still be pending or may fail without being handled before the handler returns success.

findings.title: Organization slug condition appears inverted
findings.body: The change now includes slug when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, whereas the previous logic included slug when billing was disabled. This can create or reserve an organization slug during the billing-enabled flow where only metadata.requestedSlug was expected, potentially breaking the paid slug flow.

findings.title: Webhook payload destinationCalendar changed from object/null to array
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now an array, which changes the shape of webhook payloads and other external consumers that previously received a single object or null. The tests also show inconsistent expectations between null and empty array depending on trigger, making this a public API compatibility risk.

findings.title: Missing credential causes all calendar updates to fail
findings.body: In updateAllCalendarEvents, if a booking reference has a credentialId that cannot be found in memory or in the database, credential remains undefined and updateEvent is still called. The rejected promise causes Promise.all to fail, so the catch handler returns failure for all calendar references instead of skipping only the missing credential.
